children.title: Trump orders U.S. withdrawal from the World Health Organization
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump ordered the United States to withdraw from the World Health Organization. The order also directed a pause in future U.S. funding, the recall of U.S. personnel, and an end to U.S. participation in negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement while withdrawal was pending. This action concerned WHO, not UNESCO.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive action directing the United States to withdraw from the World Health Organization. While withdrawal was pending, the order directed a pause in future U.S. funding to the organization, the recall of U.S. personnel and contractors, and a cessation of U.S. participation in negotiations on the WHO Pandemic Agreement. These are measures stated in the presidential action in connection with the withdrawal process. The order concerned the WHO specifically; it did not itself announce an immediate withdrawal from UNESCO. A later February action directed a review of U.S. participation in UNESCO and other international organizations, and UNESCO announced a separate U.S. withdrawal decision in July. The January WHO order and later UNESCO decision should therefore be recorded as separate events involving different organizations, dates and instruments. The source documents an order initiating withdrawal and setting out these administrative steps, rather than a completed withdrawal on January 20.
children.date_uncertainty: Date is the presidential action date stated in the White House document.

children.title: U.S. announces withdrawal decision from UNESCO
children.description_medium: On July 22, 2025, UNESCO announced that the United States had decided to withdraw from the organization, with withdrawal scheduled to take effect at the end of December 2026. A February 4 executive order had directed a review of U.S. participation in UNESCO and other international organizations; it was not itself an immediate UNESCO withdrawal. This decision was separate from the January WHO order.
children.description_long: UNESCO announced on July 22, 2025 that the United States had decided to withdraw from the organization again. The withdrawal was scheduled to take effect at the end of December 2026, rather than immediately on the announcement date. Earlier, a February 4, 2025 executive order had directed a review of U.S. participation in UNESCO and other international organizations. That review instruction should not be conflated with the later withdrawal decision because the two steps were distinct in timing and effect. The UNESCO action also occurred separately from President Trump’s January 20 order concerning the World Health Organization, which addressed a different international body under a separate presidential action. The supplied sources thus support a July decision announcement and a later effective date, not a January UNESCO withdrawal. The February measure was a review directive, while the July statement records the decision and its scheduled future effective date.
children.date_uncertainty: Date is UNESCO’s announcement date; the stated effective date for withdrawal is December 31, 2026.

rationale: The sources provide separate chronology, organizations and actions for WHO and UNESCO.
